title: How an Electric Toothbrush Works in 60 Seconds 🪥⚡ #shorts
description:
A sonic electric toothbrush uses a tiny electromagnet to swing its brush head side to side about 31,000 times a minute. The fast motion sweeps plaque away and even pushes fluid between your teeth, and it charges through its sealed plastic case with magnetic induction. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#electrictoothbrush #science #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A sonic toothbrush swings its bristles about *31,000 times* every minute.

steps.label: Battery
steps.text: Inside the handle, a *rechargeable battery* powers a tiny circuit board.

steps.label: Electromagnet
steps.text: The circuit flips current through a *coil* back and forth, hundreds of times a second.

steps.label: Vibration
steps.text: Magnets on the shaft get pushed and pulled, so the brush head *swings side to side*.

steps.label: Cleaning
steps.text: Fast bristles sweep away *plaque* and even push fluid *between teeth*.

steps.label: Charging
steps.text: It charges with no metal contacts. A coil in the base sends power by *magnetic induction*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Coil, magnet, *vibration*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
